claim: the lane-vocabulary commit is good and was pushed cleanly
truth: it double-encoded 74 non-ASCII characters. Get-Content -Raw in Windows PowerShell 5.1 decodes a BOM-less UTF-8 file as ANSI; writing it back as UTF-8 encodes it twice. Pushed without anyone looking at the bytes. The first repair attempt made it worse: decoding the damaged file as UTF-8 replaces the invalid bytes with U+FFFD, destroying the information before the repair runs

fix.description: restore from the last clean commit and redo the edit; never round-trip a double-encoded file. Read with [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($p)), write with [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes and UTF8Encoding $false

prevention.evidence: byte-level check before every commit: count 0xC3 followed by 0xA2 or 0x83; must be zero. Verified 0 double-encoded, 0 U+FFFD, 59 em dashes on the repair

claim: #469 fixes certification by keying on allocated guard IDs instead of label substrings
truth: FALSE. mutants-classify.mjs resolves the needle against THE MUTANT RUN'S OWN LABELS, then matches on label equality; the preflight resolves against the baseline but discards the resolved identity and passes only the needle to the worker. Stripping {id:'gNNNN'} off a guard still yields CAUGHT with id null. A plain FAIL with zero guard records yields CAUGHT via failLabels(...).includes(needle) - the ORIGINAL substring defect, still live on the fallback path. A malformed record beside a valid one also yields CAUGHT. Deleting the intended guard REMOVES the ambiguity, so the certifier is most confident exactly when the thing it certifies is most missing

claim: long messages sent to a lane were delivered
truth: they split. Typed newlines fire the composer's send, the first fragment goes and the remainder sits in the box looking sent. Four occurrences; twice reported as delivered before being noticed. A separate instance had a spend-limit modal swallow two messages entirely while every sender-side signal said delivered. The first delivery check was itself wrong: document.body.innerText INCLUDES the composer, so it reported unsent text as delivered

fix.description: compose the message as a string and insert it with document.execCommand('insertText'), which writes text WITHOUT generating keystrokes so no newline can fire a send, then click send exactly once. Post-condition check retained: subtract the composer's innerText from the page text, then match phrases from the start, both midpoints and the end

prevention.evidence: tested on a real 2858-character message full of newlines: inserted whole, sent in ONE piece, composer empty afterwards, all four probe phrases present outside the composer. The mechanism that caused the split - synthetic keystrokes - is no longer used
